What SecureBox does with your data — and what it never does.
The short, honest version of what SecureBox does.
There are no analytics, no advertising SDKs and no crash-reporting servers. Nothing is collected about you.
Scanning, traffic analysis and threat matching run locally. Your app list never leaves the phone or TV box.
The app contacts GitHub to check for updates and, if you enable it, downloads the signed Threat Intelligence feed. Both are pull-only.
Each permission is used only for the feature named on its card. SecureBox never requests SMS, call logs or contacts.
You can disable the firewall, the feed and notifications at any time. Updates always ask before installing.
SecureBox keeps optional diagnostic logs on the device. They are shared only if you export them yourself.
No security knowledge needed. Four simple steps and a plain-language glossary.
It checks the apps on this device, shows what they can access, and can stop any app from using the internet. Everything stays on your device.
Open the Threats tab and press Check now. You get a score and a short list of things to fix.
Open Apps. Each app has a score from 0 to 100. Tap an app to see what it can access and open the exact system setting to change it.
Open Network, find the app and turn on Block. Its internet is stopped locally; nothing is sent to a server.
Open Settings, then Check for updates. Updates install only after you confirm them.
A 0–100 summary of this device. Higher is better. 100 does not mean “unhackable”; it means SecureBox found no obvious risk signals.
A filter that runs on this device and stops chosen apps from reaching the internet. It never forwards your traffic.
A key that lets an app use the camera, microphone, location, contacts or another part of the device. Android controls these keys.
An app installed from a file or a store other than the Play Store. It is not automatically bad, but it was not reviewed by Google.
Code inside an app that reports what you do to an advertising or analytics company. SecureBox lists known trackers but cannot remove them.

Don\'t panic. Open the app\'s details, read the risk signals, and turn off the permission it does not need in Android settings. If you do not need the app, uninstall it. SecureBox never deletes apps for you.
Every action asks first. Turning off the firewall only stops blocking; it does not uninstall apps or erase your data.
